# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook (Wattlebridge Holdings)

## Preliminary point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" is not agreed and should be rejected

The Seller has labelled most clauses **[STANDARD]**, said they were "reviewed and cleared by both sides," and said the "disclosure framework and the limitation package" have been accepted. We have no record of any such agreement. Every [STANDARD] item departs materially from our playbook, so all of them stay open. This is the Seller's drafting position, not an agreed baseline.

**Recommendation:** Say expressly in the cover note to our mark-up that the Buyer has not accepted any categorisation, limitation package or disclosure framework, and that all clauses remain open for negotiation.

Also note that the Disclosure Letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**, about six weeks ago. We should ask for a bring-down of all specific disclosures, especially Bluefen, Riverlark and DD-006.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation: Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation: Reject. Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping basket.**
- **Reason:** The Seller's figures are five times our position, and the deductible structure removes the first AUD 250,000 of every recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months.
- **Recommendation: Reject. Counter at 24 months.**
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Also strike** the rider that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." See SPA-N-014.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years; and
  - no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: Reject outright.**
- **Reason:** If title fails, the Buyer has bought nothing. Capping title at 20% with an 18-month limit is commercially unacceptable.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out, so fraud is in effect capped and time-barred.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: Reject. Insert a full carve-out. This is non-negotiable.**
- **Reason:** The playbook says no one may waive this, and limiting liability for one's own fraud is also of doubtful enforceability.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of:
  - the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012);
  - the Accounts and statutory registers; and
  - publicly searchable records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, with each matter identified with enough detail for the Buyer to assess its nature and scope.
- **Recommendation: Reject 1.1 and 1.2. Keep only specific disclosures (paras 2–10), subject to the points below.**
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would hollow out the warranties.
- **Also qualify para 1.4** (non-admission). It must not operate to dilute the warranties or indemnities.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must:
  - be limited to named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; and
  - never exclude claims for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: Delete cl 8.3.**
- **Reason:** Combined with constructive "discoverable" knowledge, it is a second whole-data-room disclosure by the back door. It would also defeat the indemnities for matters we already know about (Ironquay, DD-006).

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Disclosure Letter:** No final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** A condition precedent requiring effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject. Make the condition a hard CP on effective consent and satisfied conditions.**
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m). Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are inadequate for a customer this material.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion." About AUD 3.2m is outstanding.
- **Disclosure Letter:** Not repaid, and no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds; and
  - effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject the post-Completion release.**
- **Reason:** A debt-free deal requires discharge at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's approval, and we have neither.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (funds flow)
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item (deducted or paid at Completion), or expressly Seller-funded with an indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Reject the silent exclusion.**
- **Reason:** The Company is the employer and will bear the cost unless the funds flow or an indemnity allocates it to the Seller.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity covering:
  - failure of transfer of SOW3 Project Materials;
  - third-party IP claims;
  - the cost of obtaining a confirmatory assignment; and
  - related loss.
  The SOW3 cure (payment of fees and assignment) should be preserved.
- **Recommendation: Reject "adequate." Broaden the indemnity and add a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable or post-Completion covenant.**
- **Reason:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, so the risk goes beyond the fee itself.
- **Do not assume** AUD 180,000 is owed or paid. DD-010 is not independent verification. Ask for Ironquay's statement or bank evidence.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (DD-006; cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - preservation of logs and evidence;
  - a completed investigation;
  - regular updates to the Buyer before Completion;
  - a pre-Completion covenant on conduct, including any notification decisions; and
  - an appropriate specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Reject the materiality characterisation. Insert investigation, preservation and update covenants plus a specific indemnity.**
- **Reason:** About 1,240 personal records were potentially exposed, and the facts are not yet established.
- **Neutral position:** Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss. Our drafting should not concede any of these either.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** The three renewals (AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Diligence on whether each renewal is:
  - unavoidable or terminable;
  - accrued or prepaid; and
  - genuinely ordinary course, given the timing and scope of the related renewals.
- **Recommendation: Reserve the position pending diligence.** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label. Equally, do not propose automatic Debt treatment or a price deduction.
- **Reason:** The facts are undetermined in both directions.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Two provisions would pull every claim into the general regime:
  - "any limitation… applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13); and
  - limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).

  Together they would pull Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment-obligation and covenant claims into the general cap, basket and time limit.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, self-contained regimes for each category, with general limitations applying only to general Warranty Claims.
- **Recommendation: Reject both default-override provisions.** Draft the general limitations to apply only to general Warranty Claims, with express exclusions.
- **Reason:** This is a hidden general-regime override, which the playbook expressly prohibits.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the DD-012 share register. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this is just the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of:
  - share issue and transfer history;
  - ASIC records;
  - a PPSR search and any encumbrance releases (note the Riverlark security);
  - the Seller's corporate authority (board resolution); and
  - share certificates.
- **Recommendation: Reject. DD-012 is not sufficient.**
- **Reason:** An internally supplied register is not independent proof of ownership, absence of encumbrances or authority.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** The tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain open and are negotiated separately from the general cap, basket and time limit.
- **Recommendation: Reject "settled." Record them as open.**
- **Reason:** These terms are unresolved. We should not concede general-regime treatment, and we should not assume unlimited liability either.

---

## Summary of actions

| # | Issue | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 001 | Cap | Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m |
| 002 | De minimis / basket | Counter at AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping basket |
| 003 | Time limit | Counter at 24 months |
| 004 | Fundamental / Title | Separate regime: 100% cap, 6+ years |
| 005 | Fraud | Full carve-out (non-negotiable) |
| 006 | Disclosure | Specific disclosure only |
| 007 | Buyer knowledge | Delete cl 8.3 |
| 008 | Bluefen | Hard CP: effective consent plus conditions satisfied |
| 009 | Riverlark | Payout letter and discharge at Completion |
| 010 | Bonuses | Line item or Seller-funded, including on-costs |
| 011 | Ironquay | Broaden indemnity, keep SOW3 cure |
| 012 | DD-006 | Covenants plus specific indemnity, neutral on facts |
| 013 | Sandbar | Reserve pending diligence |
| 014 | Categories | Strike override provisions |
| 015 | Title | Independent evidence required |
| 016 | Tax / IP | Remain open |

**Escalation:** No fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) should be offered unless Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying this draft. Please also request a bring-down of the 22 September 2026 Disclosure Letter.

- **Seller:** Two provisions would pull every claim into the general regime:

- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the DD-012 share register. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this is just the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified it.
